---
title: "Ranking noisy estimates"
subtitle: "1.3 · a simulated league, after Walters' teaching slides"
description: "Effects of unequal sampling precision on the extreme positions of a ranking."
---

High-SE estimates push small units to both ends of a ranking even when true values are unrelated to sample size.


## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **First draw.** Across 10 extreme positions, small units hold 5, medium units 4 and large units 1 (truly 3 small, 4 medium and 3 large units).
- **True values.** In the top 10 by estimate, 9 are in the true top 10; small U19 (rank 11) enters the bottom five while large U18 (rank 30) sits above.
- **Twenty replays.** Over 20 replays, small units hold 4.35 of the 10 extreme positions and large units 2.00 (7.45 in true top 10), reversing 83.9 of the 435 pairs (88.1 expected).
- **Replay 11.** Replay 11: small units hold 2, medium units 5 and large units 3.
- **Extremes highlighted.** Dashed line: the truth, 3 small and 3 large units.

Source: Simulated thirty-unit league after Walters (CCPR handout, p. 92; Mixtape slides, pp. 43–44). Standalone: [embed/noisy-league.html](../../embed/noisy-league.html). Related: [Winners' curse](winners-curse.qmd) · [Posterior shrinkage](shrinkage.qmd) · [Ranking claims](ranking-claims.qmd).
